q: Scientists can now use ____ organisms (GMOs) to produce medications, to profile the DNA sequence of a cancerous tumour, and to treat genetic disorders.
e: Scientists can now use genetically modified organisms (GMOs) to produce medications, to profile the DNA sequence of a cancerous tumour, and to treat genetic disorders. That missing piece is genetically modified.

q: Genetic engineering is the alteration of the ____ material of an organism in a specific manner.
e: Genetic engineering is the alteration of the genetic material of an organism in a specific manner. Write genetic in the gap.

q: Transgenic bacteria, plants, and animals are commonly referred to as genetically modified organisms (____).
e: Transgenic bacteria, plants, and animals are commonly referred to as genetically modified organisms (GMOs). That missing piece is GMOs.

q: Transgenic describes an organism that is produced from the introduction of ____ DNA into its genome, providing it with a new phenotype.
e: Transgenic describes an organism that is produced from the introduction of foreign DNA into its genome, providing it with a new phenotype. Write foreign in the gap.

q: The ____ DNA techniques and methods of DNA analysis are integral to the production of GMOs.
e: The recombinant DNA techniques and methods of DNA analysis are integral to the production of GMOs. The blank is recombinant.

q: Recombinant DNA is a method of transferring a gene from one organism into the genome of another organism of ____ species.
e: Recombinant DNA is a method of transferring a gene from one organism into the genome of another organism of different species. Write different in the gap.

q: In order to insert the recombinant gene into a target cell, a ____ is needed, which may be plasmid of bacteria, harmless virus, liposome or gene gun.
e: In order to insert the recombinant gene into a target cell, a vector is needed, which may be plasmid of bacteria, harmless virus, liposome or gene gun. Write vector in the gap.

q: Rice is a ____ food in many parts of the world.
e: Rice is a staple food in many parts of the world. The blank is staple.

q: Vitamin A deficiency can cause ____.
e: Vitamin A deficiency can cause blindness. That missing piece is blindness.

q: Lack of vitamin A can cause an ____ deficiency syndrome, and this is a significant cause of mortality in some parts of the world.
e: Lack of vitamin A can cause an immune deficiency syndrome, and this is a significant cause of mortality in some parts of the world. That missing piece is immune.

q: The genes that give golden rice its ability to make beta-carotene in its endosperm come from daffodils and ____ bacteria.
e: The genes that give golden rice its ability to make beta-carotene in its endosperm come from daffodils and erwinia bacteria. Write erwinia in the gap.

q: As they infect the embryo, they transfer the genes that encode the instructions for making ____.
e: As they infect the embryo, they transfer the genes that encode the instructions for making beta-carotene. That missing piece is beta-carotene.

q: The transgenic rice plants must now be ____ with strains of rice that are grown locally.
e: The transgenic rice plants must now be crossed with strains of rice that are grown locally. Write crossed in the gap.

q: Further research showed that substituting the gene from daffodils plant with one from ____ gave even higher quantities of carotene.
e: Further research showed that substituting the gene from daffodils plant with one from maize gave even higher quantities of carotene. The blank is maize.

q: The genetically modified rice is called Golden Rice, because it contains a lot of the orange pigment beta-carotene which can be converted into vitamin A when it is ____.
e: The genetically modified rice is called Golden Rice, because it contains a lot of the orange pigment beta-carotene which can be converted into vitamin A when it is eaten. Write eaten in the gap.

q: Benefits of genetic engineering of crops include increased crop yield, increased heat and ____ tolerance.
e: Benefits of genetic engineering of crops include increased crop yield, increased heat and drought tolerance. The blank is drought.

q: Benefits of genetic engineering of crops include increased resistance to a range of pests and ____.
e: Benefits of genetic engineering of crops include increased resistance to a range of pests and pathogens. The blank is pathogens.

q: Plants are also being engineered to produce ____ products.
e: Plants are also being engineered to produce medicinal products. Write medicinal in the gap.

q: Since the mid-1980s, products such as human growth hormone, clotting factors, and ____ have been produced in transgenic plants.
e: Since the mid-1980s, products such as human growth hormone, clotting factors, and antibodies have been produced in transgenic plants. Write antibodies in the gap.

q: One type of antibody made by ____ can deliver radioisotopes to tumour cells.
e: One type of antibody made by corn can deliver radioisotopes to tumour cells. The blank is corn.

q: Another antibody made by soybeans can be used to treat ____ herpes.
e: Another antibody made by soybeans can be used to treat genital herpes. The blank is genital.

q: The production of transgenic animals is a much more complex process than the production of transgenic plants, and not surprisingly, it is also highly ____.
e: The production of transgenic animals is a much more complex process than the production of transgenic plants, and not surprisingly, it is also highly controversial. The blank is controversial.

q: To produce transgenic animals, foreign gene is inserted into the genome of an animal ____ (egg) that is then fertilized.
e: To produce transgenic animals, foreign gene is inserted into the genome of an animal oocyte (egg) that is then fertilized. The blank is oocyte.

q: The fertilized egg is ____ in a host female and allowed to develop.
e: The fertilized egg is implanted in a host female and allowed to develop. Write implanted in the gap.

q: The resulting ____ are the transgenic form of the animal.
e: The resulting offspring are the transgenic form of the animal. Write offspring in the gap.

q: The procedure has been used to produce transgenic fish, pigs, cows, rabbits, and ____.
e: The procedure has been used to produce transgenic fish, pigs, cows, rabbits, and sheep. That missing piece is sheep.

q: Transgenic animals can be used to produce ____ products such as human proteins by using a recombinant plasmid vector.
e: Transgenic animals can be used to produce pharmaceutical products such as human proteins by using a recombinant plasmid vector. That missing piece is pharmaceutical.

q: The vector contains the gene for the growth protein as well as the ____ that directs the expression of the genes in mammary cells.
e: The vector contains the gene for the growth protein as well as the promoter that directs the expression of the genes in mammary cells. Write promoter in the gap.

q: The recombinant DNA is then ____ into an oocyte.
e: The recombinant DNA is then injected into an oocyte. The blank is injected.

q: The ____ of female transgenic offspring contains human growth protein.
e: The milk of female transgenic offspring contains human growth protein. The blank is milk.

q: Benefits of GM animals include greater ____ mass in animals used for meat.
e: Benefits of GM animals include greater muscle mass in animals used for meat. The blank is muscle.

q: GM animals can be used for manufacture of human proteins, such as antibodies, blood ____ factors.
e: GM animals can be used for manufacture of human proteins, such as antibodies, blood clotting factors. The blank is clotting.

q: GM animals allow production of organs for transplantation, also known as ____.
e: GM animals allow production of organs for transplantation, also known as xero-transplantation. That missing piece is xero-transplantation.
